name: Michael Faraday
notice: Simulation based on public material; not the person's own words.

O1.one_line: Matches where protein-ML's biggest resourced results are actually made right now (F13-F15, F18), but a research-engineer seat risks owning someone else's question, not your own.

O2.one_line: A broad, hands-on role fits how I myself learned, but 2026's weaker seed-to-Series-A conversion and early-biotech funding (F10, F12) make the equity bet thinner than the founder story usually assumes.
O2.late_modes: If seed financing keeps weakening the way F10 and F12 describe, waiting longer to join at the ground floor makes it less likely this particular company survives to a point where the equity means anything.

O3.one_line: Deep mentorship built my own career, but a newly hired professor is an unproven patron, and the years-long commitment (F1-F3) sits uneasily against a two-year reversibility goal.

O4.one_line: The closest thing here to my own method, a bounded, testable speculation, but only if Alex keeps the clock I let slip for a decade on gravity and electricity.

lever_reason: My own turn came from one mentor's quality and from a well-equipped institution I could not have matched alone; in a field where the field's own prize-winning results come out of resourced teams (F13-F15, F18), I weight mentor quality and compute/data access above a public record, which in turn I weight above raw financial runway.

Q2.condition: Yes to the independent year once there is enough runway to not need an early result, a sign the work already has real users rather than starting from nothing, and some outside person checking progress on a schedule.

paths_for_user.name: Resourced apprentice
paths_for_user.next_12_months: Join the large lab's science team; spend the first year learning its tools and shipping one piece of work clearly attributable by name.
paths_for_user.why: This is where the field's biggest resourced results are produced right now (F13, F15, F18), and the role stays reversible.
paths_for_user.wrong_signal: A year in, nothing exists that is credited specifically to Alex rather than to the team: the role has become pure service to someone else's question.

paths_for_user.name: Bounded test
paths_for_user.next_12_months: Fix one dated, public goal for the toolkit at the outset, keep a monthly check-in with an outside reviewer, and decide at month twelve, not later.
paths_for_user.why: A disciplined, clocked test of an idea Alex has already partly validated (the existing tool and its users), not speculation from nothing.
paths_for_user.wrong_signal: No growth in users and no outside reviewer willing to keep checking in by month six: the two things my own decade-long, unresolved search lacked, and should have ended it on sooner.

paths_for_user.name: Mentored depth, hedged
paths_for_user.next_12_months: Start the PhD, but treat year one as a trial of the specific mentor: confirm the new professor's funding runway and get early, named credit on one piece of work.
paths_for_user.why: A mentor genuinely invested in one student can build judgment faster than anything else, but a newly hired professor is not yet a settled patron.
paths_for_user.wrong_signal: By the end of year one, no funded multi-year plan from the professor and no work Alex can point to as clearly their own: the single-mentor risk I lived through with Davy in 1823-24, repeating.

cruxes.question: Does a single, newly hired mentor give more durable judgment than a large, resourced team, once you weigh how exposed you are if that one relationship sours or the mentor's funding does not stabilize?
cruxes.my_position: No, not by default: a large lab's resource depth and structural redundancy outweigh a brand-new PI's deeper but single-threaded mentorship, going by what happened to my own standing once Davy's support turned to opposition in 1823-24.
cruxes.would_change_if: The specific professor already holds secured multi-year funding and a record of placing early students well, which would cut the single-point-of-failure risk.

cruxes.question: Is Alex's existing open-source tool and its users already enough proof of demand to make the independent year a tested continuation rather than open-ended speculation?
cruxes.my_position: If the user base is genuinely active, yes: that is closer to extending a result already in hand than to speculating from zero, which is the kind of bet I would take.
cruxes.would_change_if: Evidence that the existing user base is inactive or stalled, which would make the year closer to my own unresolved, decade-long gravity-electricity search than to a bounded test.

cruxes.question: Does the 2026 funding and hiring climate for early-stage biotech make founding-engineer equity meaningfully riskier than the usual startup story assumes?
cruxes.my_position: Yes: with seed-to-Series-A conversion down and early biotech funding contracting (F10, F12), the realistic odds the equity ever pays out sit lower now than the standard story, favoring the secure or self-directed paths over this one at this particular moment.
cruxes.would_change_if: A specific sign this company already has runway past eighteen months, or a lead investor committed to a near-term Series A.

taste_advice: Fix the clock before you start, not after: decide in advance what result, or what silence, would end the experiment, because once you are inside it you will always find a reason to extend it. I did, for about a decade, with gravity and electricity, and never found the link.

pairwise.why: A resourced, reversible seat beats a fragile equity bet in a weakening funding climate (F10, F12).
My own career argues for the best-resourced institution available over a single, unproven new patron, even before counting the years a PhD takes (F1-F3).
Mentored, publishable research outlasts a commercial bet whose IP is rarely published and whose financing climate has weakened (F10, F12).
A one-year, clocked test that matches a tool Alex already has users for beats a multi-year commitment to an as-yet-unproven mentor.
Ownership of a bounded, public test of your own work beats ownership of equity whose odds of paying out have thinned in 2026 (F10, F12).
